record.paper_title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in bounded convex domains in ℂ^N
record.original_question: For a bounded convex domain Ω ⊂ ℂ^N, is visibility equivalent to the Denjoy–Wolff property for holomorphic self-maps without fixed points? That is, does Ω enjoy the Denjoy–Wolff property if and only if Ω is visible?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.9. Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain. Then Ω is visible if and only if it enjoys the Denjoy-Wolff property.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^N$ be a bounded convex domain. Equip $\Omega$ with its Kobayashi distance $k_\Omega$.

Definitions.
(a) $\Omega$ is said to be *visible* if for every pair of distinct boundary points $p, q \in \partial\Omega$ there exist neighborhoods $U_p, U_q$ in $\mathbb{C}^N$ with $\overline{U_p}\cap\overline{U_q}=\emptyset$ and a compact set $K\subset\Omega$ such that every $(1,\kappa)$-quasi-geodesic (for some fixed $\kappa\geq 0$) for $k_\Omega$ joining a point of $U_p\cap\Omega$ to a point of $U_q\cap\Omega$ intersects $K$.

(b) $\Omega$ is said to enjoy the *Denjoy–Wolff property* if for every holomorphic self-map $F:\Omega\to\Omega$ without fixed points in $\Omega$, the iterates $F^{\circ n}$ converge, uniformly on compact subsets of $\Omega$, to a constant map $z\mapsto p$ for some point $p\in\partial\Omega$.

Question. Is it true that $\Omega$ enjoys the Denjoy–Wolff property if and only if $\Omega$ is visible?
artifact.status_search_result: One direction is known: visibility of a bounded (convex) domain implies the Denjoy–Wolff property (Bharali–Maitra and related works). The converse — that the Denjoy–Wolff property forces visibility for bounded convex domains in ℂ^N — remains an open conjecture, with recent work (e.g., on failure of Denjoy–Wolff in smooth convex domains without analytic discs in the boundary) clarifying related constraints but not resolving the equivalence.

status_evidence.title: On the failure of the Denjoy-Wolff theorem in convex domains
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs a bounded convex domain in C^2 with smooth boundary, no analytic discs, and lacking the Denjoy-Wolff property; discusses relation to visibility.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work explores convex domains where Denjoy–Wolff fails, indicating the equivalence with visibility is not yet established.

status_evidence.title: A weak notion of visibility, a family of examples, and Wolff–Denjoy theorems
status_evidence.snippet: Bharali–Maitra introduce visibility and prove Wolff–Denjoy type theorems under visibility hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: The implication 'visibility ⇒ Denjoy–Wolff property' is established.

status_evidence.title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in bounded convex domains in C^N
status_evidence.snippet: States as a conjecture that for bounded convex Ω ⊂ C^N, Ω is visible iff it enjoys the Denjoy–Wolff property.
status_evidence.claim: The equivalence is presented as an open conjecture.
